email.body1:
Aaron, saw NEOGOV's EQT and CPP acquisition, the 2026 GovTech 100 spot, and the PowerDetails deal.

A new owner plus tuck-in acquisitions usually raises pipeline expectations faster than the sales team can ramp to cover. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for NEOGOV off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Aaron, quick follow-up for NEOGOV.

After a new sponsor, the board's pipeline expectations usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings NEOGOV needs across your agency base, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Aaron, last bit of proof for NEOGOV.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how NEOGOV's reply rate likely compares to other govtech software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Aaron, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority during the ownership transition, no problem at all. Timing is everything after a new sponsor, and that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to NEOGOV either way.
